{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"132128a3686f82e54d7a7bc8659782b4fce6b6d4539b3516b22416d75dead6f6","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Parking, speed restrictions and initial pedestrian duties","heading":"C2 — Parking, speed restrictions and initial pedestrian duties","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Parking, speed restrictions and initial pedestrian duties

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A03
The continued stopping-and-parking prohibition list includes the area within 30 feet of a flashing beacon, stop sign or traffic signal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes the space between a safety island or zone and the curb, plus the area within 30 feet of its end unless posted otherwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes locations within 50 feet of a rail crossing unless signs state otherwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes parking or stopping beside or opposite a road excavation or obstruction when traffic would be impeded. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes the roadway side of a vehicle already stopped or parked at the curb. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes highway bridges, elevated structures and tunnels. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes any place where stopping, standing or parking obstructs traffic flow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes the area between divided-highway roadways, including crossovers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
The continued prohibition list includes designated fire lanes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
Delaware drivers must satisfy both the general reasonable-speed restriction and specific speed limits. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A03
Drive no faster than is reasonable for the actual conditions, even when that requires traveling below the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A03
Control vehicle speed to avoid striking people, vehicles or other conveyances regardless of weather, traffic density or personal urgency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A03
Emergency conditions can change the table’s speed limits, and the posted limit must never be exceeded. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A03
The handbook’s table lists 20 mph in school zones, with a footnote referring to the code definition of when children are present. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A03
The speed table lists 25 mph for business districts, subject to emergency changes and the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A03
The speed table lists 25 mph for residential districts, subject to emergency changes and the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A03
The speed table lists 50 mph for two-lane roads, subject to emergency changes and the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A03
The speed table lists 55 mph for divided roads and roads with at least four lanes, subject to emergency changes and posted limits. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A03
The table lists 55 mph for controlled-access highways such as expressways and turnpikes, subject to emergency changes and posted limits. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A03
The table lists 65 mph for Route 1 and Interstate 495, subject to emergency changes and the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A04
Speed limits that are unsafe for prevailing conditions may be reduced, with signs showing the lower limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A04
Do not travel so slowly that normal reasonable traffic is obstructed, unless safety or legal compliance requires that speed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A04
Follow posted minimum speeds unless weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A04
Legal speed-limit signs use black lettering and numerals on white rectangles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A04
Advisory-speed signs use black lettering on yellow and often appear below warning signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A04
An advisory speed is not a specific limit, but exceeding it and crashing can support a finding that the general speed restriction was violated. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A04
Motorists share highways with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists, animal riders or drivers, and farm, road or construction machinery operators. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A04
Drivers, pedestrians and bicyclists must all follow traffic laws. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A04
Stop for a pedestrian actively crossing a marked or unmarked crosswalk; cautious progress is permitted when the pedestrian remains safely stopped on the sidewalk as required by law. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R30 | anchor: A04
Sounding the horn does not replace the duty to yield to pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R31 | anchor: A04
Be alert and yield to pedestrians with hearing impairments or physical disabilities using mobility aids or service animals, allowing for additional crossing time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R32 | anchor: A04
Do not drive through a pedestrian safety zone or block a crosswalk. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]
